title: Alphabetical sorting of Icons-and-Text Task Manager icons causes launchers to lose their position when their windows are closed
line: With alphabetical sorting, a pinned app's icon now goes back to its own place in the Task Manager after you close the app, instead of moving to the end.
explanation: Since 6.8.2 a launcher whose app has a window is hidden by a filter instead of being removed, and when the window closes the launcher comes back as a new row at the end of the model. With alphabetical sorting the task manager ordered two launchers by that row, so the launcher that came back sorted last. Manual sorting was not affected. The change orders two launchers by their position in the pinned launcher list, using the row only when that is the same.

commits.message:
libtaskmanager: keep launcher order when sorting alphabetically

With alphabetical sorting two launchers were sorted by row, and a
launcher whose window closes comes back as a new row at the end, so it
moved last. Sort launchers by launcher list position, then by row.

BUG: 528323

Same steps with the fix: after closing Dolphin its launcher is back in the first slot.

review.text: Clean fix for the exact root cause of the 6.8.2 regression in TasksModel::Private::lessThan. When separateLaunchers is enabled in non-manual sort modes, launchers that were hidden while their window was open re-enter the grouping proxy at the end, so comparing launcherPosition() before falling back to left.row() < right.row() keeps their pinned order while preserving strict weak ordering and leaving manual sort unchanged. The before/after screenshots, regression checks, and passing libtaskmanager autotests thoroughly verify the fix.

reviews.text: Clean fix for the exact root cause of the 6.8.2 regression in TasksModel::Private::lessThan. When separateLaunchers is enabled in non-manual sort modes, launchers that were hidden while their window was open re-enter the grouping proxy at the end, so comparing launcherPosition() before falling back to left.row() < right.row() keeps their pinned order while preserving strict weak ordering and leaving manual sort unchanged. The before/after screenshots, regression checks, and passing libtaskmanager autotests thoroughly verify the fix.

Correct diagnosis of the 6.8.2 regression from 'put tasks in place of their launchers': a launcher hidden by its window comes back as a new row, and the launcher-vs-launcher comparison in TasksModel::Private::lessThan used row order. Ordering two launchers by their launcher-list position (row only as tie-break) is the minimal, semantically right fix in libtaskmanager, matches the ordering already used for the mixed launcher/window cases, and leaves manual sort unchanged. Before/after screenshots and video show Dolphin returning to its slot, with multi-launcher and manual-sort regressions checked and the libtaskmanager autotests passing.
